item.title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards: The Spine of a Militarized State
item.summary: With their pervasive military, political and economic clout, the Guards are often considered the main impediment to regime change, or any change, in Iran.

item.title: A Loose Band of Emerging Powers Is Divided Over Iran
item.summary: Brazil, China and Russia all denounced the U.S.-Israeli attacks, but other nations in the BRICS group haven’t, even though Iran is a fellow member.

item.title: In War’s First Week, a Punishing Military Campaign With No Coherent Endgame
item.summary: The U.S. and Israel have pounded Iran’s leadership and undercut its defense capabilities, but President Trump has offered wildly different explanations for what he hopes to achieve.

item.title: Pakistan Praised Trump. Now It Risks Being Caught Up in His War With Iran
item.summary: U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran have set off a crippling energy crisis and sparked deadly protests in one of the world’s most populous Muslim nations.

item.title: Europe Didn’t Want War With Iran. But So Far, It Can’t Stay Out of It.
item.summary: From London to Rome and beyond, leaders are facing diplomatic headwinds and criticism at home as they take part in a conflict they did not seek.

item.title: Russia Attacks Kharkiv and Kyiv in Ukraine
item.summary: At least 10 people were killed when a Russian missile hit a five-story apartment building in the city of Kharkiv, and Kyiv and several other regions also came under attack.

item.title: For Xi, Trump’s Embrace of War Proves China Needs More Power
item.summary: China is learning lessons from the war in Iran. Chief among them, the United States may pose an even greater threat than Beijing thought.

item.title: Lebanon at ‘Tipping Point’ as It Seeks to Disarm Hezbollah
item.summary: The country is waiting to see if the government seizes on this moment to disarm the Iranian-backed armed group and how the militants will respond.

item.title: Israel Strikes Oil Facilities in Iran
item.summary: Huge flames erupted into the sky over Tehran and a nearby city on Saturday.

item.title: Iran’s De Facto Leader Says Iran Will Not Surrender or Stop Its Attacks
item.summary: Ali Larijani, the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and a close confidant of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, said Iran was determined to avenge the killing of the leader.
